facts.status_note: No source I read says whether the tower still stands, and none describes the site today or whether the public can visit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1962-63 annual report quoted by Canada Lookouts says the smokejumpers erected the tower in 1962. The listing's note dates a Junction Ranger Tower in the Nisbet Forest to about 1916. The sources do not say whether that is the same structure, so the story uses 1962 and reports the note.

notes_for_editor: Two pages read: the Canada Lookouts Nisbet Forest entry (1962 and 1963 annual-report quotes) and the Saskatchewan tower listing (coordinates matching the brief, 80 ft heavy steel, a 1916 Junction Ranger Tower note). The 1916 note conflicts with the 1962 erection and is not explained. The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency, formerly Dept. of Natural Resources) does not appear in any text I read. The listing's Fishers Tower entry mentions a 1958-1963 Nisbet Forest tower and is not used. A uer.ca thread on Saskatchewan towers (cupolas removed, cameras installed) returned HTTP 403 and may or may not concern Nisbet. I did not check firelookout.ca for a Nisbet record. Fate and present condition are unknown.
